best_plan.name: p4
best_plan.rationale: p4 gave the best overall trade-off: the highest observed quality (f1_score 0.9474) while staying much cheaper and faster than the broad sem_filter+sem_join alternative (p2). It beat p1 on quality and beat p2 dramatically on cost/latency by first restricting to one movie, mapping sentiment once, filtering to positive reviews, and only then doing the join over a much smaller candidate set.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model evolved from simple per-operator averages to record-scaled estimates, which made it clear that sem_join was the dominant cost and latency driver, especially when fed many candidate pairs. That pushed plan design toward reducing pair counts before joining: sem_map on the already filtered movie subset was relatively cheap, while sem_filter/sem_join over larger sets was expensive. Among the tested options, the cheapest high-quality pattern was exact movie filter -> sentiment sem_map -> exact sentiment filter -> sem_join.

plan_codes.p1:
reviews = load_data("Reviews.csv")

pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", reviews)
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{
        "name": "sentiment",
        "type": str,
        "description": "Overall sentiment of the review toward the movie. Output exactly one word: positive or negative."
    }],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.project(["idx", "reviewId", "sentiment"])

other = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name + "_rhs", "Reviews.csv", reviews)
other.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
other.sem_map(
    [{
        "name": "sentiment",
        "type": str,
        "description": "Overall sentiment of the review toward the movie. Output exactly one word: positive or negative."
    }],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
other.project(["idx", "reviewId", "sentiment"])

pipeline.sem_join(
    other,
    "The two rows have the same sentiment label, meaning both are positive or both are negative.",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE
)
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["reviewId"] < row["reviewId_right"])
pipeline.project(["idx", "reviewId", "reviewId_right"])
pipeline.limit(10)
pipeline
